I will plant all 3.5 mu with spring maize, because that is the crop I know best and it fits my land, water access, and household labor situation. Some people in my family work off-farm, so I will keep the plan simple and steady rather than doing anything complicated. I will use hybrid seed because I care most about stable yield on a small farm. I will do rotary tillage since it is practical for me at the start of the season and helps me prepare the field quickly. I will put on a moderate amount of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium so the maize can establish well and fill grain without overspending. Since I have a well, I will irrigate a few key times if the weather is dry, especially around emergence and later growth stages. I will spray pesticides only when needed, and I will keep the number of applications limited because I want to control costs and labor. My goal is a stable, reliable harvest rather than taking big risks.
